markdown.markdown:
This page contains selected resources to support **ECN 4199: Industrial Data Analytics**.

Use these resources when you need extra help with:

- Python
- Google Colab
- pandas
- data visualization
- machine learning
- forecasting
- NLP and generative AI

Do not try to watch everything.

Use resources strategically.

---

# 1. How to Use This Page

Each resource is linked to a specific part of the course.

| Course Area | Use These Resources When |
|---|---|
| Google Colab | You are struggling to open or run notebooks |
| Python Basics | You are confused about variables, lists, loops, or functions |
| pandas | You are working with datasets |
| Visualization | You are creating graphs |
| Machine Learning | You are learning prediction, classification, or clustering |
| Forecasting | You are working with time-series data |
| NLP and AI | You are working with text and generative AI |

---

# 2. Google Colab

Google Colab is the main coding environment used in the first part of this course.

## Recommended Video

[Google Colab Beginner Tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JJYZ3OE_lGo)

Use this if you are confused about:

- opening notebooks
- running code cells
- saving notebooks
- using Colab in the browser

## Alternative Beginner Tutorial

[Getting Started with Python in Google Colab](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZAhmF30S4M)

Use this if you want a newer beginner-friendly introduction.

---

# 3. Python Fundamentals

Python is the core programming language used in this course.

## Recommended Full Beginner Course

[Learn Python — Full Course for Beginners](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rfscVS0vtbw)

Use this for:

- variables
- data types
- lists
- loops
- functions
- beginner syntax

## Python for Data Science

[Python for Data Science — Course for Beginners](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LHBE6Q9XlzI)

Use this when you want a broader introduction to Python for data analysis.

---

# 4. pandas for Data Handling

pandas is the main Python library for working with datasets.

## Recommended Playlist

[Corey Schafer — Pandas Tutorials](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL-osiE80TeTsWmV9i9c58mdDCSskIFdDS)

Use this for:

- importing datasets
- DataFrames
- selecting columns
- filtering rows
- cleaning data
- handling missing values

## Specific Data Cleaning Video

[Python Pandas Tutorial — Cleaning Data](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KdmPHEnPJPs)

Use this for Week 4.

---

# 5. Data Visualization

Visualization is essential for understanding and communicating economic patterns.

## Matplotlib Playlist

[Corey Schafer — Matplotlib Tutorials](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL-osiE80TeTvipOqomVEeZ1HRrcEvtZB_)

Use this for:

- line graphs
- bar charts
- scatter plots
- labels
- figure customization

## Full Matplotlib Tutorial

[Matplotlib Full Course](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wB9C0Mz9gSo)

Use this if you want a longer explanation.

---

# 6. Machine Learning Concepts

Machine learning is introduced from Week 8 onward.

## Recommended Conceptual Channel

[StatQuest with Josh Starmer](https://www.youtube.com/c/joshstarmer)

Use this for simple explanations of:

- regression
- logistic regression
- decision trees
- random forests
- PCA
- K-means clustering

## StatQuest Machine Learning Playlist

[StatQuest Machine Learning Playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLblh5JKOoLUIcdlgu78MnlATeyx4cEVeR)

Use this when you need conceptual clarity before coding.

---

# 7. scikit-learn

scikit-learn is used for machine learning models.

## Full Practical Course

[Machine Learning with Python and Scikit-Learn](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hDKCxebp88A)

Use this for:

- train/test split
- linear regression
- classification
- model evaluation
- machine learning workflows

---

# 8. Classification, Clustering, and PCA

These topics appear in Weeks 9 and 10.

## StatQuest Topics

Use StatQuest for:

- logistic regression
- decision trees
- random forests
- K-means clustering
- PCA

[StatQuest Video Index](https://statquest.org/video-index/)

This is useful when you need a specific topic quickly.

---

# 9. Time Series Forecasting

Forecasting is covered in Week 11.

## Beginner Time Series Forecasting Course

[Time Series Forecasting in Python — Tutorial for Beginners](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fxx_E0ojKrc)

Use this for:

- time series data
- baseline forecasts
- ARIMA intuition
- forecasting workflow

## Written Companion Resource

[Learn Time Series Forecasting in Python](https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/learn-time-series-forecasting-in-python/)

Use this if you prefer a written explanation.

---

# 10. NLP and Generative AI

Week 12 introduces text analytics and generative AI.

## Suggested Search Topics

Use these search phrases carefully:

```text
Python NLP beginner tutorial
TextBlob sentiment analysis tutorial
Natural Language Processing for beginners
Prompt engineering for beginners
```

Important:

Do not blindly trust AI-generated explanations.

Always verify:

- facts
- code
- citations
- economic interpretation

---

# 11. Official Documentation

Official documentation is useful when you want precise syntax.

| Tool | Documentation |
|---|---|
| Python | [Python Documentation](https://docs.python.org/3/) |
| pandas | [pandas Documentation](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/) |
| matplotlib | [Matplotlib Documentation](https://matplotlib.org/stable/) |
| Plotly | [Plotly Python Documentation](https://plotly.com/python/) |
| scikit-learn | [scikit-learn Documentation](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/) |
| statsmodels | [statsmodels Documentation](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/index.html) |
| Google Colab | [Google Colab FAQ](https://research.google.com/colaboratory/faq.html) |

---

# 12. Recommended Learning Strategy

Do not watch resources passively.

For every video:

1. Open your notebook
2. Type the code yourself
3. Change the numbers
4. Break the code intentionally
5. Fix the error
6. Write one economic interpretation

Passive watching does not build skill.

---

# 13. Minimum Resource Path

If you are falling behind, follow this minimum path:

| Week | Resource |
|---|---|
| Week 1–2 | Google Colab tutorial |
| Week 3 | Python beginner course |
| Week 4 | pandas playlist |
| Week 5–6 | Matplotlib and Plotly documentation |
| Week 7–10 | StatQuest |
| Week 11 | Time series forecasting tutorial |
| Week 12 | NLP + AI guide |

---

# 14. Important Warning

Do not confuse watching tutorials with learning.

You learn by:

- writing code
- making mistakes
- debugging
- interpreting results
- explaining findings in economic language

The goal of this course is not to become a YouTube learner.

The goal is to become an economist who can use computational tools critically.
